your_book:
Friday was a split-tape day for Jaleel's book, with the biggest winners and biggest loser sitting side by side. ServiceNow (NOW, +7.44%) and Adobe (ADBE, +6.1%) were the standout movers, likely driven by strong earnings momentum and short-covering respectively — together they added meaningful ground on a portfolio-weighted basis. Abbott (ABT, +2.29%) and Lululemon (LULU, +3.3%) also contributed positively. Against that, Rocket Lab (RKLB, -8.69%) was the session's ugly number — down nearly 9% on Friday alone and now sitting at a -30.1% open loss on an 8.5% book weight, rated AVOID with a QARP of just 46.4. That is the portfolio's sharpest internal contradiction. Uber (UBER, -4.31%) also pulled back, adding to an existing -7.9% open loss despite a Strong Buy rating.

The drift problem is concentrated in three names. RKLB is the clearest case: price and thesis are moving in opposite directions, and the system itself is flagging AVOID. ADBE's +6.1% Friday pop is welcome, but the -8.2% open loss and the flagged AI-disruption narrative mean one good day doesn't resolve the thesis question — the story, not the numbers, still drives this one. BSX is drifting quietly: it gained +1.54% Friday, but it carries an elevated guidance-slash flag, a -7.6% open loss, and an earnings event in just two trading sessions (July 29).

Watch BSX into Tuesday's print very closely — guidance was already cut to flat through Q3, so the bar is low but the risk of a further reset is real. RKLB needs a decision, not a watch. And LULU's +3.3% Friday should not be mistaken for a reversal; the guidance-cut flag, -10.6% open loss, and stalled Americas comps remain firmly in place heading into the September 2 next catalyst.

attention.note: The system rates this AVOID with a QARP of 46.4, yet it sits at 8.5% of the book with a deepening loss; the gap between rating and position size demands a hard exit decision, not continued monitoring.
